title: Finish3D parallel toolpath does not pass smoothly over model holes
body:

The Finish3D parallel toolpath stops, picks up, or behaves unexpectedly over model holes. The land model (fill_openings) lids closed openings narrower than a stated width. But holes wider than the width, open holes, and holes at lid edges still cause stops and picks.

Expected:

The Finish3D parallel toolpath should pass over holes as if they are not there. The tool should fly over every hole smoothly at a consistent height. No stops. No picks. No weird behavior over hole regions.

Done means:

- The Finish3D parallel path passes over all holes without retract or plunge moves over hole regions
- No stops or picks over hole regions
- The path verifies cleanly against the real model

body:
Asked for by Mike (collaborator) on 2026-11-18: SolidCraft shows "update available" in its title bar; a click downloads the latest version and installs it. CamCraft has nothing like it - a user only finds a new release on GitHub.

Wanted:
1. **Check:** at start (and at most once a day), read the latest release tag from GitHub (`api.github.com/repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/releases/latest`). No account, no telemetry; a setting turns it off; offline or rate-limited = silent, never an error dialog. Never in the browser (wasm) build.
2. **Show:** a small "Update available: vX.Y.Z" item at the right of the title bar, next to the version (#352). Its tooltip names the version and links the release notes.
3. **Install on click** - the hard part, because the app is running:
   - Download the asset for this platform (Windows zip/installer, macOS, Linux tar/AppImage, FreeBSD) to a temp folder and check its SHA-256 against the release (the release needs a checksum file - today it has none) before anything runs.
   - Unsaved work: ask to save first (the usual unsaved-changes prompt); never drop work.
   - Replace and restart: a running exe cannot be overwritten on Windows. Usual pattern: quit, let a small helper (or the installer itself) swap the files and start the new version; or rename the running exe aside and put the new one in place, then restart. Package-manager installs (AUR, Homebrew, a .deb) are not self-updated: show "update available" with the command to run instead.
   - Failure at any step leaves the old version working and says what failed.
4. Never auto-install without a click; never download in the background without the setting allowing it.

Done means: on Windows and one of macOS/Linux, a build that is one release behind shows "Update available", a click updates it and restarts on the new version with the project reopened; a corrupt download (bad checksum) is refused with a message and the old version still starts; with the setting off or offline, nothing is shown and nothing fails.

Clean-room note: this is ordinary desktop-app behaviour (no Autodesk material involved). SolidCraft (our sister project) is a reference for the user experience only.

A new page in the user guide (site/content/guide/, linked from the install page and the FAQ), plain language:

1. **The app does not start or closes at once:** start it with another graphics backend - a shortcut with `--gpu-backend dx12`, `vulkan` or `gl` added to Target. What each means, in one line each.
2. **The whole PC freezes, the screen shows "snow"** (seen on a desktop Ryzen 5 with onboard Radeon): this is a graphics driver or hardware hang that CamCraft's 3D view triggers, not a CamCraft crash. 3. **Testing the PC itself:** free tools by name and what each tests - MemTest86 (RAM, from USB), OCCT (CPU/RAM/graphics with temperatures), HWiNFO64 (temperatures). Note: save work first.
4. **What to send us:** `dxdiag` -> "Save All Information" (note it contains the PC name), the CamCraft log file and where it is (once #2421 lands), the version, and the step where it failed. Where to send it (GitHub issue or Discord).
5. **Windows on ARM / virtual machines:** the x64 build runs under emulation; it worked on a Parallels ARM VM using the software renderer, slower.

Done means: the page exists in the guide, is linked from the install page, and builds with `zola build`. No claims we have not tested; tools are named, not endorsed.

body:
A Windows 11 user reported that v0.23.0 "kept crashing" and uninstalled it. We had nothing to go on: no log, no GPU, no step.

A check on a second Windows 11 machine (Intel Arc 140T + NVIDIA RTX 5050 laptop, v0.23.0 zip) found the app runs there with the default, dx12 and vulkan backends, so the crash is likely tied to the user's GPU/driver. It also found:

- The adapter/backend line ("gpu: using/adapter ...") is printed to **stdout only**. It is not in the log file. A user who launches from the Start menu and sends us their log cannot tell us which GPU path crashed.

Wanted (smallest useful set):
1. The chosen adapter (name, vendor, driver, backend) and the list of adapters found are written to the log file at startup.
2. A panic, or a wgpu device/surface error at startup, is written to the log file with its message and a backtrace, before the process exits.
3. The log file's location is easy to find (e.g. named in the About/Help dialog, or printed in the crash message).
4. If startup fails on one backend, the error says which `--gpu-backend` values to try.

Done means: launching on Windows without a terminal leaves a log file that names the adapter and backend, and a forced startup failure (e.g. `--gpu-backend` set to a backend the machine lacks) leaves its error in that log. Pinned by a test of the log setup where it can be tested headlessly.

body:
Split out of #2389 (P1). The generation side of #2389 is fixed on `issue/2389-tilt-heights-axis`: a tilted operation's reference heights (Top/Bottom of stock, Top/Bottom of model, Work offset) are now read along the turned tool axis (`camcraft_app::operation::fold_height`). The display was not changed there.

What still happens (from #2389's investigation):
- `crates/ui/src/interact.rs` `height_planes` / `height_plane_lines` draw the Clearance/Retract/Top/Bottom planes as horizontal rectangles at the setup Z, across the stock's XY box. They do not read the tilt.
- `crates/ui/src/operations.rs` `height_echo` prints "(= Z ...)" from `resolve_height`, the setup-Z resolve. For a tilted op on an asymmetric stock this number is not the value generation uses.
- `operation::region_z` (used by `interact.rs`, `boundary_viz.rs`, `boundary_draft.rs`) also reads the setup Z for a tilted op.

Expected: for a tilted op, each plane stands at right angles to the tool axis, at the distance `fold_height(...) - origin.z` along it from the plane origin, over the stock's extent in the plane's local XY (`TiltedFrame::to_world`). The echo states the value along the tool axis (e.g. "(= 5.000 along tool axis)") from the same `fold_height` call generation makes.

Repro: `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj`, "Flat A90" > Heights tab (the planes lie flat above the bar). On that symmetric bar the numbers agree; on an asymmetric stock (#2390) they do not.

Done means: the viewport planes and the "(= ...)" text of a tilted op use the op's frame and `fold_height`; a ui law test pins a tilted plane's corners and the echo value on an asymmetric stock; untilted planes and text unchanged.

body:
Reported by the maintainer (2026-11-17, while reading `examples/first-4axis-part`): "A turns.. the heights doesnt follow.. so they dont 'tilt with' A". Filed by an agent for him; not yet reproduced by the filer.

## What happens

An op with a tilt (`params.*.tilt.a_deg`, the 3+1/3+2 index) is planned in its rotated frame: its geometry is read into the tilt frame (pinned by `crates/app/tests/fourth_axis_pose.rs`, `crates/app/tests/area_controls.rs` tilted-pocket tests). Its heights are not: clearance, retract, top and bottom stay world-Z values while the plane tilts with A.

The shipped example cannot show it: the bar in `examples/first-4axis-part` is round and centred on the A axis, so the skin is the same distance from the axis at every A, and the world-Z clearance `G0 Z0.875` is safe on all four sides by coincidence (`examples/first-4axis-part.nc`, every block after `G0 A-90/A0/A90/A180`).

## Why P1

On any part whose sides differ (square or offset stock, an off-centre feature, a fixture, flats at different depths) the clearance and retract planes of an indexed side are in the wrong place for that side. A rapid at "clearance" can then run into stock or part on that side and pass verify, because the heights the verifier reads are the same wrong ones. A collision that passes is P1 by AGENTS.md.

## Expected

Each height of a tilted op is stated in that op's own frame (measured along its tool axis from its own top / stock), converted with the same frame as its geometry, and the rapid/clearance laws judge the converted values. Untilted ops are unchanged.

## Done means

- A pinning test on a non-symmetric part: square (or offset) stock on the microARC 4, flats at different depths on two indexed sides; for each side the posted clearance and retract Z equal that side's own top + the op's height offsets, not the A0 side's.
- The same test fails on main today (mutation check).
- A rapid from clearance on the far side of an offset stock is refused (or cleared) by verify, never passed silently.
- `examples/first-4axis-part` stays byte-identical or changes only where the heights now follow its tilt (round bar centred on A: it should not change).

Related: #2390 (make the 4-axis example asymmetric; hold it until this is fixed, so the example pins the corrected heights), #763 (one machining-frame seam), #2135 (the example).

title: Post: a generic LinuxCNC mill post (3-axis), separate from the Tormach PathPilot post

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
### What are you trying to do

I run a 3-axis mill on LinuxCNC 2.9 (Remora controller, `M6` remapped to an automatic tool changer) and would like to post from CamCraft straight to it. There is no plain LinuxCNC post today. The Tormach PathPilot post is the closest, but it carries Tormach assumptions, so its output has to be checked and hand-edited before it is safe on a stock LinuxCNC machine. #435 / #495 is one example: the retract assumed machine Z0 is the top of travel.

### How you imagine it working

A generic LinuxCNC mill post (e.g. `linuxcnc.cps` plus a `linuxcnc-3axis.mch` machine), written to the RS274NGC dialect as LinuxCNC documents it, with no PathPilot-specific codes. LinuxCNC machines differ a lot from one another, so the machine-specific parts would be options rather than fixed:

- **Retract and tool-change position:** `G53 G0 Z<value>` with a user value (machine Z0 is not always the top of travel), `G28`/`G30`, or none.
- **Tool change:** `T<n> M6` then `G43 H<n>`, with an option to leave out `G43` when the `M6` remap applies the tool length itself.
- **Path blending:** `G64 P<tolerance>` with a user value, or `G61` exact path.
- **Program start/end:** a safe block (`G17 G90 G40 G49 G80`, units, work offset); end with `M5 M9` and `M2` or `M30`; optional `%` delimiters.
- **Drilling and tapping:** `G81`/`G82`/`G83`/`G73`. LinuxCNC's rigid tap is `G33.1`, which needs a spindle encoder, so an option to refuse or expand taps on a machine without one.
- **Arcs:** `G2`/`G3` with incremental IJK (LinuxCNC's default `G91.1`), helices allowed.
- Comments in parentheses, no line numbers by default; spindle `M3`/`M4 S`, coolant `M7`/`M8`/`M9`.

Happy to run posted programs through a LinuxCNC 2.9 sim and air-cut them on my machine, and report back.

body:
**The request (mkinney, 2026-11-15):** make sure the post-merge gate runs to completion even when more merges arrive, using the one-line change below.

## What happens

`.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: post-merge-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && 'main' || inputs.ref || 'main' }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

Each PR merge is its own push to main and starts its own run. With `cancel-in-progress: true`, each new merge cancels the run in progress. In a merge batch (N merges within one gate run, about 37 min), only the LAST run finishes:
- #1752: seven runs in a row were cancelled by later merges. The breaking merge had to be found by hand in a range of 6 merges, including the cut merge.
- #1909 and #1856 (2026-11-15): after the 10-PR bulk batch, the only result was for the tip. Each needed a manual search for the cause (#1839, and #1787 with #1793).

## Proposal (one line)

```yaml
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

With a concurrency group, GitHub keeps at most one run in progress and one pending:
- The run already in progress always finishes. It gives a full result for its commit.
- A newer merge waits as the single pending run. A still newer merge replaces it, so runs do not pile up.

For a batch of N merges this tests 2 points (the first merge and the last), not 1. Each run gives a result. The cost: more runner time on the self-hosted post-merge runner (no billed minutes), and the result for the batch tip arrives up to one gate-run later.

The comment at the top of the file (line 9, "tests only the newest head (cancel-in-progress)") must change with it. The cut-skip logic (`post-merge-skip.sh`) does not change.

## Later options (not part of this issue)

- A unique group per commit (no cancels at all): every merge is tested, but a 10-PR batch takes about 6 h on one runner.
- Bisect-when-red: when a run fails, test the merges between the last green run and this one, to find the breaking merge automatically.

## Done means

`cancel-in-progress: false` is on the post-merge concurrency group, the comment explains the queue behaviour, and a batch of merges shows the in-progress run finishing (not "cancelled") in the Actions history.

A `.github/` workflow change: the maintainer's decision. Agents do not edit it.

title: Fanuc lathe G76: four schedule readings are unverified; a wrong Z-shift or end-Z reading moves a flank thread axially or into a shoulder

body:
## What is open

The Fanuc lathe post (`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`) can write the two-block G76 thread cycle (post option G76 cycle). The post models the control's pass schedule from public Fanuc-compatible references (GSK988TA manual, LinuxCNC G76 for the flank sign). No source that we read states four readings of that schedule. No run on a Fanuc control or on a Fanuc simulator confirms them. The PathPilot Hub simulation cannot check them, because its lathe uses the LinuxCNC one-block `G76 P.. J.. K..`.

Found in the full review of PR #517 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/517#pullrequestreview-5910390160). The readings are recorded in `docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`.

In the table, k is the thread height and a is the tool angle of the first block (twice the flank angle).

| Item | Reading that the post uses | What a wrong reading can do | Threads affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Z-shift sign, and which pass sits at the programmed Z | Deeper passes move in the direction of travel (LinuxCNC sign). The post sets the start Z to `c_first - k*tan(a/2)`, so pass n starts at `start + depth_n*tan(a/2)`. | The whole thread moves axially by `k*tan(a/2)` to `2k*tan(a/2)`. For the golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (2 mm lead) that is 0.6 to 1.25 mm. This is a cut in the wrong place. | Flank threads only (a not 0) |
| 2. End-Z shift | Each pass ends at the programmed end Z. | If the control also shifts the end of each pass by `depth*tan(a/2)`, the root pass ends `k*tan(a/2)` past the end Z. At a shoulder, the tool can cut into the shoulder. | Flank threads only (a not 0) |
| 3. Minimum-depth clamp | Q(dmin) is a per-pass minimum against the previous clamped depth. | The pass count or the per-pass depth changes. The root does not change. The control can cut fewer, deeper passes than the verdict judged (the tool load is not judged). | Constant-area ladders. Equal-depth ladders (the default) are not affected. |
| 4. Rounding | Words are whole least increments. R comes from the rounded ladder and is refused beyond one increment. | The pass count is fixed. Single rungs of a long sqrt ladder can differ from the laid ones by a few increments. This is not a gouge. | Long sqrt ladders |

The default radial thread (a = 0) has no Z shift. Items 1 and 2 do not change it. Main already writes the flank angle and the flank start (#416). Thus this risk is on main now. PR #517 does not add it.

## Priority

`P3`. A wrong reading of item 1 or 2 is wrong posted G-code (a `P1` class). But no source shows that the reading is wrong, and the defect is not shown. A workaround exists: the default output is the G32 chain, which does not use the control's schedule, and the default infeed is radial. If a control run shows that item 1 or 2 is wrong, raise this issue to `P1`.

## Open question (do not implement here)

Must the Fanuc post refuse, or warn, for a flank-angle G76 (a not 0) until items 1 and 2 are verified? A refusal makes the output safe now, but it removes a cycle that can be correct. A warning keeps the cycle but can be ignored. Decide this before the control run, or with its result.

## Done means

- A run on a Fanuc lathe control, or on the vendor's simulator, posts the goldens `thread_g76.nc` (mm and inch) and `thread_g76_area.nc`.
- The run records, for each pass: the start Z, the end Z and the depth.
- Each of the four items is confirmed, or the post is changed to the control's reading with a pinning test.
- `docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md` (or a new decision entry) records the result.
- The open question above has a recorded answer.

body:
Requested by the maintainer.

## 1. Simulation shows the tool and holder as spun profiles
While simulating, draw the **tool and its holder as revolved bodies**: the half-profile spun about the spindle axis, at the tool's position and orientation each frame. Today's simulation doesn't show them as solids. Use the same profile the collision laws judge (the revolved envelope, #368), so what you see is what is checked.

## 2. Imported tool bodies and holders become an editable half-profile
When a tool body or holder is imported as **STEP**, convert it to a **2D half-profile on a centreline** (the meridian of the revolved envelope: radius against height along the tool axis). Store it as a **DXF**, with the centreline as its own entity/layer, so the profile can be edited (in the spun-profile editor, #93) and re-exported.

- Only the half-profile is editable, and the body is always its revolution about the centreline.
- Conversion should be conservative: the profile is the outer envelope (max radius at each height), never smaller than the solid, so collision checks stay safe. Non-revolved features (flats, coolant holes, the holder's drive slots) are enveloped, never cut away. Say so in the UI.
- Refuse by name when the STEP body has no clear axis (axis detection/alignment: #370) instead of guessing one.
- A tool/holder can also be **imported directly as a DXF half-profile** (a centreline plus an open profile on one side of it).
- DXF read/write is our own, written from the published DXF reference (entities `LINE`, `ARC`, `LWPOLYLINE`, layers). The minimum needed is lines and arcs, with a named refusal for anything else (splines, unclosed profiles that cross the centreline).

## Related
- #93 spun (revolved-profile) design editor for tool and holder shapes: the editor for these profiles.
- #361 import vendor STEP tool models; #368 a vendor holder judged by its revolved envelope (closed); #370 align a vendor STEP by its tool coordinate systems; #371 pick tip and axis on an imported body (closed).
- Fixtures get the same treatment in a sibling issue.

## Done means
- The simulation draws the tool and holder as revolved solids from their profiles (structural/paint assertion where possible, hand-tested by the maintainer; no snapshot PNG changes).
- Importing a STEP holder produces a DXF half-profile with a centreline, and the envelope encloses the original solid (a test samples the STEP mesh and checks every point lies inside the revolved profile).
- A DXF half-profile imports as a tool/holder body; malformed DXF (no centreline, spline, crossing profile) is a named error in a test, never a panic.
- Round trip: STEP → DXF → body → DXF is stable within tolerance.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
